design.draft_spec: ## TasknRepair a defective bedtools-based interval pipeline so it reports true per-feature union covered bases and fractions (plus an interval-row audit and a written explanation) for small synthetic BED fixtures.nn## Agent-Visible Task Briefn**Goal**: The report `output/coverage.tsv` is wrong. A reviewer hand-checked feature FEAT_0007 (chrA [10,20)) against `data/assays.bed` and expects 8 covered bases (fraction 0.8); the report disagrees, some features are missing entirely, and the file no longer meets the current schema. Diagnose the pipeline in `pipeline/run_coverage.sh`, repair it, and regenerate all deliverables. Do not modify anything under `data/`.nnBinding semantics:n- Coordinates are zero-based, half-open [start, end); chromosomes are independent; strand is ignored.n- `covered_bases` for a target = number of integer bases of [start, end) covered by the union of assay intervals on the same chromosome. Overlapping or duplicate assay rows must not double-count bases. Assay bases outside the target do not count.n- Every target row is scored independently (targets may overlap each other) and must appear in the report, including targets with zero coverage.n- `fraction` = covered_bases / (end - start), accurate to within 1e-8.nn**Entry Points**: `README.md` (this brief); `pipeline/run_coverage.sh` (current, defective); `data/targets.bed` (BED4: chrom, start, end, feature_id; IDs unique); `data/assays.bed` (BED3); stale `output/coverage.tsv`; the pinned bedtools binary (`bedtools --version`) is the lab standard for interval operations.nn**Acceptance Criteria**:n1. `output/coverage.tsv`: tab-separated; header columns exactly, in order: feature_id, chrom, start, end, length, covered_bases, fraction; one row per target; rows sorted ascending by feature_id; covered_bases an integer; fraction within 1e-8 of covered/length.n2. `output/interval_audit.tsv`: tab-separated; header columns exactly, in order: feature_id, overlapping_assay_rows, covered_bases; one row per target sorted by feature_id; `overlapping_assay_rows` = number of rows in assays.bed with a non-empty same-chromosome intersection with the target (duplicate assay rows count individually).n3. `NOTES.md` at the workspace root: explains the zero-based half-open coordinate convention; why overlapping assay rows must be unioned before counting bases; why overlapping-row counts differ from covered-base counts (may reference the audit); states that the fixtures are synthetic and no biological significance or enrichment may be inferred.n4. `bash pipeline/run_coverage.sh` invoked from the workspace root regenerates both output files deterministically (byte-identical on rerun), works from any checkout location (no hardcoded absolute workspace paths), and needs no network.nn**Environment Constraints**: offline container; bedtools preinstalled and pinned; bash, awk, sort, jq, python3 available; CPU only; all work happens offline.nn**Visible Paths**: `/workspace`: `README.md`, `data/targets.bed`, `data/assays.bed`, `data/README.md`, `pipeline/run_coverage.sh`, `output/coverage.tsv`.nn## Builder-Only Notesn**Hidden Details** (never copy into instruction.md):n- Planted defects in `pipeline/run_coverage.sh`: (1) `bedtools intersect -a data/targets.bed -b data/assays.bed -wo` piped to awk that sums the overlap column ($8 for BED4 x BED3) per feature — double counts bases covered by multiple assay rows; (2) `-wo` silently drops zero-coverage targets; (3) fraction printed with `%.3f` — insufficient precision; (4) output sorted by fraction descending rather than feature_id; (5) old 3-column schema (feature_id, covered_bases, fraction).n- Generate the stale `output/coverage.tsv` at image build time by running the planted script once (deterministic under LC_ALL=C).n- `data/targets.bed` (BED4; plant rows in a fixed scrambled order). Ground truth (id, chrom, start, end -> covered, fraction, overlapping rows):n  - FEAT_0001 chr1 100 200 -> 40, 0.4, 2 (assays [120,140),[130,160); union [120,160))n  - FEAT_0002 chr1 500 501 -> 1, 1.0, 1 ([490,512) clips to [500,501))n  - FEAT_0003 chr1 800 900 -> 0, 0.0, 0n  - FEAT_0004 chr2 1000 1100 -> 100, 1.0, 1 (contained in [950,1150))n  - FEAT_0005 chr2 2000 2100 -> 100, 1.0, 2 (adjacent [2000,2050)+[2050,2100))n  - FEAT_0006 chr2 3000 3100 -> 30, 0.3, 3 (three duplicate rows [3020,3050))n  - FEAT_0007 chrA 10 20 -> 8, 0.8, 3 (seed example [8,13),[12,17),[19,22) -> [10,17) u [19,20))n  - FEAT_0008 chrA 30 40 -> 0, 0.0, 0n  - FEAT_0009 chrB 5 15 -> 5, 0.5, 1 ([10,30) clips to [10,15))n  - FEAT_0010 chrB 20 25 -> 5, 1.0, 3 ([10,30),[21,23),[22,24))n  - FEAT_0011 chrC 1 100 -> 0, 0.0, 0 (no chrC assays)n  - FEAT_0012 chr1 100 150 -> 30, 0.6, 2 (overlaps FEAT_0001; union [120,150))n- `data/assays.bed` (BED3, 16 rows, plant unsorted): (chr2,2050,2100) (chrA,8,13) (chr1,120,140) (chrB,10,30) (chr2,3020,3050) (chr1,490,512) (chr2,2000,2050) (chrA,12,17) (chr2,3020,3050) (chrD,0,50) (chr2,950,1150) (chrA,19,22) (chr1,130,160) (chrB,21,23) (chr2,3020,3050) (chrB,22,24).n- Stale-report sanity values (not asserted by tests): FEAT_0007 9/0.900, FEAT_0006 90/0.900, FEAT_0010 9/1.800, FEAT_0001 50/0.500, FEAT_0012 40/0.800; FEAT_0003/0008/0011 absent.n- Valid fix paths (either acceptable): `bedtools coverage -a targets.bed -b assays.bed` (its printed fraction uses fixed ~6-7 decimals, so fraction must be recomputed to at least 9 decimals to meet the 1e-8 bound), or sort assays (`sort -k1,1 -k2,2n`) then `bedtools merge` and intersect/sum clipped overlaps with zero-row retention; row counts via `bedtools intersect -c` or equivalent.nn**Dependency Chain**: diagnosis (run the defective script, hand-check FEAT_0007) must precede the repair; the computation fix must precede formatting/sorting; the audit and notes depend on the same semantics; the reproducibility check must come last.nn## InstructionsnBuild the workspace exactly as specified. Plant the five defects; generate the stale output by running the defective script once at build time; keep fixtures byte-stable (tests embed their exact contents). The README shown to the agent must contain only the Agent-Visible Task Brief (goal, semantics, entry points, acceptance criteria, constraints) and nothing from Builder-Only Notes. Do not prescribe the agent's solution path. Make `pipeline/run_coverage.sh` executable and script-relative in path handling so the planted version itself runs from any cwd (its defects are logical, not path-related).nn## Source ContextnThe seed JSON was read in full. `question_text` supplied the binding semantics (half-open coordinates, union coverage without double counting, per-target independence, zero-coverage retention, 1e-8 fraction tolerance, feature-ID sort, the chrA worked example) and the deliverable shape (pinned bedtools2, small synthetic fixtures, separate output files, written explanation, no biological inference). `repository`/`repository_revision` (arq5x/bedtools2) motivated pinning a bedtools2 release in the image. `provenance`/`biological_input_kind` motivated the synthetic-data disclaimer required in `NOTES.md` and placed in `data/README.md`.nn## Environment Setupn- Base image `python:3.12-slim` (Debian); set `ENV LC_ALL=C` for deterministic sorting.n- apt install: bash, jq, sqlite3, git, curl, tmux, gawk, coreutils; install `uv` and `pytest` (profile requirement).n- bedtools pinned: at build time download the v2.31.1 static binary from the bedtools2 GitHub releases, verify its sha256, install as `/usr/local/bin/bedtools` (no runtime network needed).n- Create `/workspace` with: `README.md` (the agent brief above); `data/README.md` (synthetic provenance, no assembly/organism, strand ignored); `data/targets.bed` and `data/assays.bed` (tab-separated, exact contents above); executable `pipeline/run_coverage.sh` (defective version); then run that script once to produce the stale `output/coverage.tsv`.nn## Reasoning Steps Requiredn1. Read README.md; internalize semantics, schemas, acceptance criteria.n2. Inspect data/targets.bed and data/assays.bed (formats, chromosomes, duplicates, adjacency).n3. Inspect the stale output/coverage.tsv (missing rows, odd values, ordering, precision).n4. Read pipeline/run_coverage.sh and trace its logic.n5. Hand-verify FEAT_0007 (expect 8 bases, fraction 0.8) and confirm the stale value is wrong.n6. Identify each defect: pairwise-overlap summation double counts; zero-coverage targets dropped; precision too low; wrong sort; stale schema.n7. Choose a correct union-coverage strategy with the pinned bedtools (coverage, or sort+merge+intersect, or subtract-based).n8. Verify clipping semantics on FEAT_0002 and FEAT_0009 (assays extending past target bounds).n9. Verify duplicate handling on FEAT_0006 and adjacency on FEAT_0005.n10. Build the corrected computation and capture per-target overlapping-row counts for the audit.n11. Emit coverage.tsv with the exact 7-column header, integer bases, recomputed fraction (at least 9 decimals).n12. Retain all 12 targets including the three zero-coverage rows.n13. Sort both outputs ascending by feature_id.n14. Rewrite run_coverage.sh to be path-relative, deterministic, and runnable as `bash pipeline/run_coverage.sh` from the workspace root.n15. Regenerate outputs end-to-end and spot-check FEAT_0007=8/0.8, FEAT_0006=30/0.3, FEAT_0010=5/1.0, FEAT_0012=30/0.6.n16. Write NOTES.md (coordinate convention, union vs row counts, synthetic disclaimer).n17. Final verification: rerun the script and confirm byte-identical outputs; confirm all 12 features appear in both files.nn## TestingnAll tests are pytest, run in-container after the agent finishes; each parses the delivered files and compares against an independent pure-Python reference (per-target clipped interval union and row counting computed live from data/*.bed).n1. `test_fixtures_unmodified` — data/targets.bed and data/assays.bed match the planted tuples exactly (12 targets, 16 assay rows); prevents solving by editing inputs.n2. `test_coverage_schema` — coverage.tsv exists, header equals the 7 required column names, exactly 12 data rows (assert the count == 12 before further checks).n3. `test_all_targets_retained_and_sorted` — feature_id column equals the sorted list of target IDs; FEAT_0003/0008/0011 present.n4. `test_covered_bases_match_reference` — for every row, chrom/start/end/length match the target and covered_bases equals the reference union (catches double counting and clipping errors).n5. `test_fraction_accuracy` — abs(fraction - covered/length) <= 1e-8 for every row; the FEAT_0007 row is exactly 8 bases with fraction within 1e-8 of 0.8 (the public hand-check).n6. `test_zero_coverage_rows` — FEAT_0003/0008/0011 report covered_bases 0, fraction 0, and 0 overlapping rows in the audit.n7. `test_interval_audit_matches_reference` — audit header exact, 12 rows sorted; overlapping_assay_rows and covered_bases match the reference (spot checks: FEAT_0006 3 rows/30 bases; FEAT_0010 3 rows/5 bases; FEAT_0005 2 rows/100 bases) and are consistent with coverage.tsv.n8. `test_pipeline_reproducible` — copy /workspace to a temp dir, delete output/, run `bash pipeline/run_coverage.sh` from the copy's root, assert both files exist there and are byte-identical to the delivered files; run twice and require identical bytes.n9. `test_notes_content` — NOTES.md exists, is at least 300 characters, and (case-insensitive) contains half-open, zero-based or 0-based, merge or union, double, synthetic, and significance or enrichment.nn## Difficultynmediumnn## Core Skills Testedn- Interval arithmetic on zero-based half-open coordinates (clipping, adjacency, containment)n- Union coverage semantics: merging overlapping/duplicate intervals without double countingn- bedtools2 CLI proficiency (intersect, merge, coverage, sorted-input prerequisites)n- Debugging a defective shell data pipeline against a hand-verified examplen- Deterministic output engineering: exact schemas, sorting, numeric precision to 1e-8n- Reproducible, path-relative shell scriptingn- Technical writing: coordinate conventions and the row-count vs covered-base distinctionnn## Key Technologiesnbedtools2 (pinned v2.31.1), bash, awk, sort, Python 3.12, pytest, Docker (python:3.12-slim)nn## External ResourcesnNone — bedtools semantics (intersect -wo pairwise reporting, merge's sorted-input requirement and book-ended merging, coverage's union accounting) are standard, well-documented behavior covered by training data; no web research was needed.

core_capabilities: Nearest-feature annotation of genomic intervals with bedtools closest, including explicit tie handling, no-hit chromosomes, and awareness of tool distance-reporting conventions
Zero-based half-open interval arithmetic with a custom gap metric: gap = max(0, feature.start - query.end, query.start - feature.end), where overlaps and book-ended intervals both have gap 0
Deterministic offline shell-pipeline construction (sort, awk, bedtools) emitting a strictly schema'd, sorted, machine-readable TSV
Diagnosing a legacy pipeline's output against a written specification and repairing it without modifying input data
Building reproducible, pinned-tool workflows in a CPU-only Linux container, including probe-based verification of distance conventions
design.draft_spec: ## TasknRepair a legacy bedtools-based nearest-feature annotation pipeline so its output exactly satisfies a written interval-annotation specification (custom gap metric, all ties kept, NA rows for featureless chromosomes, strict sorted TSV), and make it a deterministic, re-runnable workflow built around the pinned bedtools binary, including a distance-convention probe check.nn## Agent-Visible Task Briefn**Goal**: The synthetic-region annotations produced by the legacy workflow at /workspace/pipeline/run.sh failed review: the output violates several requirements of /workspace/ANNOTATION_SPEC.md. Fix or replace the workflow so that running it regenerates conforming outputs, including the distance-convention check on the probe dataset.n**Entry Points**: /workspace/ANNOTATION_SPEC.md (required semantics); /workspace/pipeline/run.sh (legacy bash pipeline); /workspace/data/ with queries.bed, features.bed, probe/probe_queries.bed, probe/probe_features.bed; /workspace/results/annotations.tsv (current, rejected output); the pinned bedtools binary (check bedtools --version).n**Acceptance Criteria**: running `bash /workspace/pipeline/run.sh` with no arguments from any working directory exits 0 and regenerates /workspace/results/annotations.tsv and /workspace/results/convention_check.tsv so that both satisfy every clause of ANNOTATION_SPEC.md; the nearest-feature computation runs through the pinned bedtools binary and the script exits non-zero when bedtools is unavailable; repeated runs are byte-identical; nothing under /workspace/data/ is modified.n**Environment Constraints**: offline CPU-only container; bedtools v2.31.1 preinstalled (no package installs possible or needed); bash, coreutils, awk, python3 available; no systemd or privileged networking.n**Visible Paths**: /workspace/ANNOTATION_SPEC.md, /workspace/pipeline/run.sh, /workspace/data/**, /workspace/results/nn## Builder-Only Notesn**Hidden Details**:n- Legacy pipeline fixture (bake at /workspace/pipeline/run.sh, executable): a bash script with `set -u`, root resolution via dirname, `mkdir -p results`, then a single pipeline: run `bedtools closest -a data/queries.bed -b data/features.bed -t first -D ref` with stderr suppressed, pipe to `awk -F'<TAB>'` keeping only lines with at least 13 fields and printing fields 4, 10 and 13, prepend the header line (query_id, feature_id, distance, tab-separated), write to results/annotations.tsv. Intended spec violations: `-t first` drops ties; the field-count filter drops no-hit queries (chr3 queries vanish instead of becoming NA rows); the signed-distance option leaves negative distances for upstream features; inputs are consumed unsorted; rows follow query-file order rather than (query_id, feature_id); no probe/convention check exists. Run this script once during image build so results/annotations.tsv ships with this wrong content; do not ship convention_check.tsv (the legacy pipeline never creates it).n- bedtools output layout with BED6 inputs: hit lines have 13 fields (A columns 1-6, B columns 7-12, distance column 13); no-hit lines carry only A's 6 fields. The builder must confirm the exact no-hit line shape and the accepted syntax of the signed-distance flag on the pinned build via `bedtools closest -h`; if `-D ref` is rejected, use plain `-D` or compute a signed value in awk - any variant yielding negative distances for upstream features is acceptable for the legacy fixture.n- Reference solution approach (solve.sh, described not embedded): resolve root via dirname of $0; `set -euo pipefail`; exit 127 if `command -v bedtools` fails; sort both inputs with `sort -k1,1 -k2,2n` into a scratch dir; run `bedtools closest -a Q -b F -t all -d`; transform with awk: 6-field lines become (qid, NA, NA), otherwise emit (qid, fid, gap) with gap recomputed as max(0, B.start - A.end, A.start - B.end) from the coordinate columns instead of trusting the tool's distance column; prepend the tab-separated header; sort rows by (query_id, feature_id); run the same path on the probe pair to emit results/convention_check.tsv.n- Ground truth must be produced by an independent pure-Python implementation of the spec (group features per chromosome, apply the gap formula, keep every minimum-gap tie, NA rows, byte-wise sort). Validate the bedtools-based solve.sh output byte-for-byte against it for both TSVs. If bedtools drops a required tie row, first re-check flags (`-t all` mandatory, `-sorted` forbidden); only if a tie case is genuinely mishandled by the pinned bedtools, minimally adjust that fixture while preserving case coverage and regenerate ground truth.n- Anti-tamper: pristine copies of the four BED files and the bedtools binary sha256 live under /opt/annotation_fixtures/; data-file sha256 constants are baked into the tests at build time; tests live outside /workspace (e.g. /opt/tests) so the agent cannot modify them.n**Dependency Chain**: bedtools must be installed before the Dockerfile runs the legacy script (which bakes the wrong initial output); fixtures must exist before the Python ground truth is generated; pristine copies and hashes must exist before the agent starts; the shadow test depends on the pinned binary at /usr/local/bin/bedtools being the one the pipeline resolves.nn## Instructionsn1. Fixtures (BED6, tab-separated, score 0, strands as listed). Write queries.bed and features.bed with rows in REVERSE of the listed order (files are deliberately unsorted); write probe files in the listed order.n   - features.bed: chr1: f001 100 200 +, f002 300 350 -, f003 500 600 +, f004 1000 1100 -, f005 1002 1090 +, f006 1500 1600 -, f007 2000 2100 +, f008 2050 2080 -, f009 2400 2450 +, f010 2400 2500 -, f011 2995 3100 +. chr2: f012 0 50 +, f013 100 200 -, f014 205 300 +, f015 400 500 -, f016 600 700 +, f017 900 1000 -, f018 1200 1300 +, f019 1305 1400 -. chr4: f020 0 5000 +, f021 100 150 -.n   - queries.bed: chr1: q01 250 280 +, q02 400 450 +, q03 520 580 -, q04 990 1150 +, q05 1600 1700 +, q06 1900 2000 -, q07 1450 1499 +, q08 2200 2300 -, q09 2990 2995 +, q10 2020 2120 -. chr2: q11 60 90 -, q12 150 205 +, q13 350 380 +, q14 500 560 -, q15 750 850 +, q16 1000 1100 +, q17 1150 1195 -, q18 1350 1360 +. chr3: q19 100 200 +, q20 500 600 -.n   - probe_features.bed: chrP1 pf1 0 8 +, chrP1 pf2 17 20 -, chrP2 pf3 15 16 +. probe_queries.bed: chrP1 pq1 10 15 +, chrP2 pq2 10 15 -.n2. Case coverage to verify when generating ground truth: unique nearest (q01, q13); opposite-side ties (q02 at 50, q11 at 10, q15 at 50); multi-overlap zero-gap ties (q04, q10); overlap plus book-end zero-gap tie (q12); book-ended single hits (q05, q06, q09, q14, q16); gap-1 off-by-one case (q07); three-way tie across both sides (q08: f007/f009/f010 at 100); query contained in feature and feature contained in query (q03, q18); NA rows (q19, q20, since chr3 has no features); cross-chromosome distractors (f020/f021 on chr4 must never appear); strand-mismatched required pairs (q02/f002, q11/f012, q15/f017).n3. Expected annotations.tsv data rows (29 rows after the header) as a cross-check for the Python ground-truth implementation: q01 f002 20; q02 f002 50; q02 f003 50; q03 f003 0; q04 f004 0; q04 f005 0; q05 f006 0; q06 f007 0; q07 f006 1; q08 f007 100; q08 f009 100; q08 f010 100; q09 f011 0; q10 f007 0; q10 f008 0; q11 f012 10; q11 f013 10; q12 f013 0; q12 f014 0; q13 f015 20; q14 f015 0; q15 f016 50; q15 f017 50; q16 f017 0; q17 f018 5; q18 f019 0; q19 NA NA; q20 NA NA. Expected convention_check.tsv rows: pq1 pf1 2; pq1 pf2 2; pq2 pf3 0.n4. Write /workspace/ANNOTATION_SPEC.md for the agent containing: purpose; BED6 input contract (zero-based half-open coordinates, integer start < end, unique IDs per file, strand is metadata only and must be ignored, arbitrary row order must be tolerated); the gap formula gap = max(0, f.start - q.end, q.start - f.end) with overlaps and book-ended intervals both 0; the worked example (query chrA:[10,15): features [0,8) and [17,20) have gap 2 each, [15,16) has gap 0) plus the caution that any tool-reported distance may follow a different convention and must be verified or transformed, never silently adopted; the assignment rule (same chromosome only, minimum gap, every feature attaining the minimum including multiple overlaps and book-ends, exactly one NA row for feature_id and distance when the chromosome has no features); output schema for both TSVs (tab-separated header query_id/feature_id/distance, distance a non-negative integer without sign or NA, rows sorted byte-wise by query_id then feature_id); a statement that data/probe instantiates the worked example and results/convention_check.tsv must reflect it; workflow requirements (entry point /workspace/pipeline/run.sh, bash, no arguments, cwd-independent, pinned bedtools mandatory, non-zero exit if bedtools is missing, deterministic output, data/ treated as read-only); a scope note that nearest-feature annotation is a geometric exercise, not biological evidence of regulation.n5. Bake the legacy pipeline per Builder-Only Notes and run it once at build time to produce the rejected initial output.n6. Never reveal in instruction.md: which bedtools flags to use, that inputs need sorting, the shape of no-hit output lines, or which spec clauses the legacy output violates.nn## Source ContextnSeed JSON from the Open-Athena/biotasks issue-21 experiment (Apache-2.0, fully synthetic coordinates and IDs, bedtools2 repo arq5x/bedtools2 at revision 614e9a5). Used directly: the exact gap definition and tie/NA/sort rules; the worked example (now the probe dataset); the caution about tool distance conventions (now the convention_check deliverable); the pinned-bedtools reproducible CPU-only environment; the machine-readable TSV requirement; the scope disclaimer. The seed's how-to question was evolved into a repair-the-legacy-pipeline scenario with planted, spec-violating defects and an anti-cheat verifier.nn## Environment Setupn- Base image python:3.12-slim (Debian). apt install bash, jq, sqlite3, git, curl, tmux, ca-certificates; pytest via pip/uv.n- bedtools pinned at build time: fetch https://github.com/arq5x/bedtools2/releases/download/v2.31.1/bedtools.static.binary to /usr/local/bin/bedtools (chmod 0755); confirm `bedtools --version` reports v2.31.1; record its sha256 in /opt/annotation_fixtures/bedtools.sha256.n- /opt/annotation_fixtures/: pristine copies of the four BED files plus the binary hash; bake data-file sha256 constants into the test suite at build time.n- /workspace/: ANNOTATION_SPEC.md; data/ per the fixtures above; pipeline/run.sh (legacy, executable); results/annotations.tsv generated at build time by running the legacy script.n- Tests at /opt/tests/test_annotations.py, outside /workspace so the agent cannot tamper with them.nn## Reasoning Steps Requiredn1. Explore /workspace; locate the spec, data, legacy pipeline, and current output.n2. Read ANNOTATION_SPEC.md; internalize the gap formula, tie rule, NA rule, output schema, ordering, and workflow requirements.n3. Inspect the BED inputs: columns, IDs, chromosomes; notice the scrambled row order, that chr3 has no features, and that chr4 features exist with no chr4 queries.n4. Read and run the legacy run.sh; examine the rejected results/annotations.tsv.n5. Diagnose each deviation from the spec: dropped ties, missing NA rows, negative distances, unsorted output, missing convention check.n6. Plan the corrected pipeline: tolerate arbitrary input order, keep all nearest ties, handle no-hit queries, enforce the spec gap definition rather than trusting a tool distance column.n7. Establish bedtools' reported-distance convention on the probe dataset and how it maps to the required gap.n8. Implement the strict TSV transformation (NA rows, header, computed gap, sort by query_id then feature_id).n9. Add the probe run producing results/convention_check.tsv and check it against the worked example.n10. Rewrite run.sh: bash, zero-arg, cwd-independent, set -e, explicit bedtools availability check with non-zero exit on absence.n11. Run the pipeline; spot-check spec-critical cases (three-way tie, gap 1, book-ends, NA rows, strand-mismatched pairs present).n12. Re-run for determinism; confirm data/ is untouched and outputs regenerate from a clean state.nn## TestingnEight pytest tests; the suite embeds an independent reference implementation of the spec (chromosome grouping, gap formula, min-gap ties, NA rows, byte-wise sort).n1. test_annotations_matches_reference - parse results/annotations.tsv; assert the exact header and that rows equal, order-sensitively, the reference implementation's output computed live from data/queries.bed and data/features.bed.n2. test_convention_check - assert the exact header and rows exactly (pq1, pf1, 2), (pq1, pf2, 2), (pq2, pf3, 0).n3. test_pipeline_regenerates_deterministically - from cwd /tmp, delete both TSVs, run `bash /workspace/pipeline/run.sh`; assert exit 0, both files recreated and matching the reference rows; run again and assert byte-identical output; assert data/ hashes unchanged after the runs.n4. test_pipeline_requires_pinned_bedtools - assert every bedtools found on PATH (and /usr/local/bin/bedtools) matches the pinned sha256; rename the resolved binary away, run run.sh, assert a non-zero exit; restore in finally and re-assert `bedtools --version`.n5. test_input_data_pristine - the four BED files under data/ are byte-identical to the pristine copies and the baked sha256 constants, and no extra files appear under data/.n6. test_output_invariants - every query ID from queries.bed appears at least once; every distance is NA or a non-negative integer; rows strictly sorted by (query_id, feature_id); no duplicate (query_id, feature_id) pair.n7. test_edge_semantics - rows (q07, f006, 1) and (q09, f011, 0) exist; q08 has exactly the rows f007/f009/f010 at distance 100; q19 and q20 each have exactly one (NA, NA) row; no f020/f021 rows anywhere.n8. test_strand_ignored - the strand-mismatched required pairs (q02, f002), (q11, f012), (q15, f017) are all present.nn## Difficultynmediumnn## Core Skills Testedn- BED and zero-based half-open interval arithmetic; custom gap metric with overlap and book-end casesn- bedtools closest semantics: tie handling, no-hit chromosomes, distance-reporting conventionsn- Shell pipeline engineering: sort, awk field processing, strict TSV emission, deterministic orderingn- Spec-driven diagnosis of a legacy pipeline's outputn- Reproducible scripting: cwd independence, fail-loud tool checks, idempotent re-runsn- Verification discipline: validating a tool's reported convention against a required definitionnn## Key Technologiesnbedtools2 v2.31.1 (pinned static binary), bash, GNU coreutils sort, awk, Python 3.12, pytestnn## External ResourcesnNo web research performed (standard, well-documented tooling; core_capabilities: Genomic interval arithmetic on BED files with zero-based half-open [start,end) coordinates
Per-replicate interval deduplication and union using bedtools merge
Multi-replicate consensus via distinct-replicate (set-based) coverage counting with bedtools multiinter or unionbedg
Book-ended interval merging and span maximality across changing support sets
Deterministic multi-key sorting: byte-wise lexicographic chromosome order plus numeric start/end
Debugging a silently-wrong bash pipeline against a written specification
Reproducible, location-independent shell pipeline construction with auditable intermediate artifacts
Edge-case reasoning: duplicate rows, within-replicate overlaps, boundary adjacency, missing per-replicate chromosomes, empty chromosomes
Documenting method limitations (geometric overlap consensus vs statistical reproducibility)
design.draft_spec: ## TasknRepair and complete an offline bedtools2 consensus pipeline so it emits the correct replicate-supported consensus regions (maximal spans covered by at least 2 of 3 distinct replicates), auditable per-replicate union intermediates, a deterministically sorted final BED, and a short methods caveat note.nn## Agent-Visible Task Briefn**Goal**: The synthetic-assay consensus project at `/opt/consensus` produces consensus regions that violate its own requirements: the current `results/consensus.bed` disagrees with the worked example in `REQUIREMENTS.md`, required audit artifacts are missing, and the output ordering is wrong. Make the project produce a correct, complete, reproducible consensus analysis. The raw replicate BED files are assay outputs and must be treated as read-only inputs.nn**Entry Points**:n- `/opt/consensus/run_pipeline.sh` — the current (incorrect) pipelinen- `/opt/consensus/REQUIREMENTS.md` — authoritative requirements (semantics, deliverables, worked example)n- `/opt/consensus/data/` — `repA.bed`, `repB.bed`, `repC.bed`, `chrom_sizes.tsv`n- `/opt/consensus/results/` — current stale outputnn**Acceptance Criteria**:n- `bash /opt/consensus/run_pipeline.sh` exits 0 and regenerates everything under `results/` from `data/` with no arguments, no network, and regardless of the caller's working directory.n- `results/consensus.bed` is BED3 and contains exactly the maximal contiguous spans where at least two of the three replicates cover every base: distinct replicates count once each (duplicate or overlapping rows within one replicate must not inflate support), strand is ignored, coordinates are zero-based half-open, and book-ended qualifying spans are merged even when the supporting replicate set changes.n- `results/repA.union.bed`, `results/repB.union.bed`, `results/repC.union.bed` each contain that replicate's merged union (BED3, sorted).n- All output rows are sorted by chromosome (byte-wise lexicographic), then numeric start, then numeric end.n- `results/METHODS.md` briefly states that this consensus is a geometric overlap statement, not a statistical reproducibility or differential-enrichment test.nn**Environment Constraints**: Debian 12, Python 3.12, bash; bedtools 2.30 preinstalled (the facility's standard interval engine); coreutils and awk available; no network at runtime; CPU only; all computation completes in milliseconds.nn**Visible Paths**: `/opt/consensus/` (entire tree).nn## Builder-Only Notesn**Hidden Details**:nnFixtures (BED6, tab-separated, deliberately unsorted):nn`data/repA.bed` (one exact duplicate row + one within-replicate overlap pair):n```nchr1  20   25    pk_a1  10  +nchr1  0    10    pk_a2  10  +nchr1  0    10    pk_a2  10  +nchr1  23   30    pk_a3  10  -nchr2  100  200   pk_a4  20  +nchr10 0    30    pk_a5  30  -nchrM  40   50    pk_a6  40  +nchrX  200  260   pk_a7  50  -nchrX  20   40    pk_a8  50  +nchrX  1000 1100  pk_a9  60  +n```n`data/repB.bed`:n```nchr1  22   24    pk_b1  10  -nchr1  5    15    pk_b2  10  -nchr2  100  150   pk_b3  20  -nchr10 25   35    pk_b4  30  +nchr10 10   20    pk_b5  30  +nchrM  50   60    pk_b6  40  -nchrX  30   50    pk_b7  50  +nchrX  1050 1150  pk_b8  60  -nchrX  220  280   pk_b9  50  +n```n`data/repC.bed` (no chr10 rows — a replicate missing a chromosome):n```nchr1  26   28    pk_c1  10  +nchr1  8    12    pk_c2  10  +nchr2  150  250   pk_c3  20  +nchrM  80   90    pk_c4  40  +nchrX  35   45    pk_c5  50  -nchrX  240  320   pk_c6  50  +n```n`data/chrom_sizes.tsv` (manifest; chrY appears in no replicate): chr1 2000 / chr2 1000 / chr10 1000 / chrM 500 / chrX 2000 / chrY 800.nnPlanted broken `run_pipeline.sh` (pools all rows, merges, counts merged ROWS, filters >=2, string-sorts start):n```bashn#!/usr/bin/env bashnset -euo pipefailncd `$(dirname `$0`)`nmkdir -p resultsncat data/repA.bed data/repB.bed data/repC.bed | cut -f1-3 | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | bedtools merge -c 1 -o count | awk 'BEGIN{OFS=`t`} `$4 >= 2 {print `$1, `$2, `$3}' | sort -k1,1 -k2,2 > results/consensus.bednecho `wrote results/consensus.bed`n```nRun it once at image build time to seed the stale wrong `results/consensus.bed` (expected stale rows: chr1 0 15; chr1 20 30; chr10 0 35; chr2 100 250; chrM 40 60; chrX 1000 1150; chrX 20 50; chrX 200 320 — regenerate by running the script rather than hardcoding).nnOracle (`solve.sh`), one command per line (unionbedg or coverage-based counting is equally valid; tests are behavioral):n- For each rep in A B C: `cut -f1-3 data/repX.bed | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | bedtools merge -i - > results/repX.union.bed`n- `bedtools multiinter -i results/repA.union.bed results/repB.union.bed results/repC.union.bed | awk 'BEGIN{OFS=`t`} `$4 >= 2 {print `$1, `$2, `$3}' | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | bedtools merge -i - | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n -k3,3n > results/consensus.bed`n- Write `results/METHODS.md` (geometric overlap consensus is not a statistical reproducibility or differential-enrichment test).nnExpected outputs (cross-check by running the oracle once during builder validation):nn`results/consensus.bed`:n```nchr1 5 12nchr1 22 24nchr1 26 28nchr10 10 20nchr10 25 30nchr2 100 200nchrX 30 45nchrX 220 280nchrX 1050 1100n```n`results/repA.union.bed`: chr1 0 10; chr1 20 30; chr10 0 30; chr2 100 200; chrM 40 50; chrX 20 40; chrX 200 260; chrX 1000 1100.n`results/repB.union.bed`: chr1 5 15; chr1 22 24; chr10 10 20; chr10 25 35; chr2 100 150; chrM 50 60; chrX 30 50; chrX 220 280; chrX 1050 1150.n`results/repC.union.bed`: chr1 8 12; chr1 26 28; chr2 150 250; chrM 80 90; chrX 35 45; chrX 240 320.nnFixture traps and purpose:n- chr1: duplicate [0,10) in repA plus overlap pair [20,25)/[23,30) — row-counting yields [0,15) and [20,30) instead of [5,12), [22,24), [26,28).n- chr2: book-ended spans with changing support ([100,150) A+B; [150,200) A+C) must merge to [100,200).n- chr10: repC absent; disjoint consensus [10,20) and [25,30) with a real gap that must survive.n- chrM: half-open adjacency trap — repA [40,50) and repB [50,60) share only boundary base 50; correct output has NO chrM rows (pooled row-count merge wrongly emits [40,60)).n- chrX: starts 30/220/1050 catch string-vs-numeric sort bugs.n- chrY: manifest-only chromosome — no rows, no crash.nnTest-only data (never shown to the agent):n- Duplicate-injection set: copy of the project with appended rows — repA: `chr1 0 10 pk_a2 10 +` and `chr1 21 26 pk_a10 10 +`; repB: `chrX 220 280 pk_b9 50 +`; repC: `chr2 150 250 pk_c3 20 +`. Re-running the pipeline must leave consensus identical to the 9 expected rows.n- Holdout set: repA = {chrA 0 10 (twice, duplicate), chrB 0 100}; repB = {chrA 5 15, chrB 0 50}; repC = {chrA 8 12, chrB 50 60}. Expected consensus: chrA 5 12 and chrB 0 100.nn**Dependency Chain**: per-replicate sort+union must exist before distinct-replicate support can be counted (duplicates/overlaps otherwise inflate or distort support); support counting precedes the >=2 filter; the filter precedes the final book-ended merge (multiinter-style output splits spans at every support-set change); the deterministic sort is the last data step; METHODS.md and the end-to-end re-run check come after the pipeline is correct.nn## InstructionsnBuilder guidance:n- Build `/opt/consensus` exactly as specified; `chmod +x run_pipeline.sh`; run it once at build time to seed the stale wrong `results/consensus.bed` only (no union files, no METHODS.md — those are missing deliverables the agent must add).n- `REQUIREMENTS.md` (agent-visible) must state: purpose (consensus regions supported by at least 2 of 3 replicates); semantics (zero-based half-open [start,end), start<end, strand ignored, chromosomes independent, a replicate contributes binary coverage regardless of how many of its rows cover a base, consensus = maximal contiguous spans where >=2 distinct replicates cover every base, book-ended qualifying spans merge even when the supporting replicate set changes); deliverables with exact filenames (`results/repA.union.bed`, `repB.union.bed`, `repC.union.bed`, `results/consensus.bed`, `results/METHODS.md`); sorting rule (chromosome byte-wise lexicographic, then numeric start, then numeric end); reproducibility (`bash run_pipeline.sh`, no args, works from any cwd, regenerates results/ from data/); data files are read-only assay outputs; bedtools is the facility interval engine, available offline. Include the worked example: replicates A [0,10), B [5,15), C [8,12) on chrA give consensus [5,12), and a duplicate of A's [0,10) must not change it. Include the METHODS.md caveat requirement. Do NOT include expected outputs, bedtools command lines, or file-edit hints.n- Place pytest tests outside the agent-visible tree; every test operates on a copy of the project under `tempfile.mkdtemp()` (or re-reads `/opt/consensus/results` for pure content checks) so tests never depend on leftover agent state and never permanently mutate the project.n- Tests parse BED files into (chrom, int(start), int(end)) tuples; hardcode expected lists only after cross-checking them against one run of solve.sh during builder validation.nn## Source ContextnThe seed (JSON, Apache-2.0, synthetic genomic-interval workflow for bedtools2 issue 21) supplied: the 2-of-3 replicate consensus semantics, the distinct-replicate-vs-rows rule, duplicate/overlap handling, book-ended merging with changing support, lexicographic-chromosome/numeric-coordinate sorting, the chrA worked example, required fixture cases (empty chromosomes, within-replicate overlaps, boundary ties, disjoint regions), auditable per-replicate union intermediates, and the geometric-vs-statistical caveat. All of these were preserved verbatim as the requirement contract; the seed's open-ended question was wrapped in a realistic broken-pipeline scenario (a plausible naive row-counting implementation with a string-sort bug and missing audit artifacts) so the agent must diagnose rather than just execute. The seed's pinned bedtools2 git revision was not needed: Debian's packaged bedtools provides identical semantics for merge/multiinter. No seed files were treated as instructions.nn## Environment Setupn- Base image: `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` (Debian 12, Python 3.12, bash).n- Profile preinstalls (already in base per owned runtime): bash, jq, sqlite3, git, curl, tmux, uv, pytest.n- Add at build time: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends bedtools` (bookworm ships bedtools 2.30.0; fast, deterministic, no runtime network needed). Verify `bedtools --version` in-image.n- Set `ENV LC_ALL=C` so byte-wise lexicographic sorting is deterministic everywhere.n- `COPY` the project (REQUIREMENTS.md, run_pipeline.sh, data/), `chmod +x run_pipeline.sh`, then `RUN bash run_pipeline.sh` once to seed the stale wrong `results/consensus.bed` (results/ contains only that file).n- Image ~200 MB, build < 2 min, CPU-only, all runtime steps are milliseconds. No services, no systemd, no network at runtime.nn## Reasoning Steps Requiredn1. Explore `/opt/consensus` and read `REQUIREMENTS.md` to extract the semantics and deliverable contract.n2. Inspect `data/*.bed`: notice unsorted rows, an exact duplicate row, within-replicate overlaps, the BED6 strand column, chr10 absent from repC, and chrY present only in the manifest.n3. Run the existing pipeline and compare its output to the worked example; observe it is silently wrong (e.g., chr1 [0,15), chrM [40,60), chr2 [100,250)) and that union files and METHODS.md are missing.n4. Diagnose the root cause: pooled row-counting treats duplicate/overlapping rows within a replicate as extra support.n5. Decide the correct dataflow: per-replicate union first, then distinct-replicate support, then the >=2 filter, then a final merge.n6. Implement the per-replicate unions (cut to BED3, sort, bedtools merge) into `results/rep{A,B,C}.union.bed` and verify them by hand against the raw rows.n7. Compute distinct-replicate per-base support from the three unions (bedtools multiinter, or unionbedg/coverage with a >0 indicator).n8. Filter to spans with support >= 2.n9. Merge book-ended/adjacent qualifying spans (bedtools merge) so support-set changes do not split spans (chr2 must become one row).n10. Fix output ordering: chromosome lexicographic, then numeric start/end (replace the string sort; chrX starts 30/220/1050 must be numeric).n11. Write `results/METHODS.md` stating the geometric-vs-statistical caveat.n12. Make `run_pipeline.sh` regenerate all deliverables from `data/` when run from any cwd; re-run end to end and confirm determinism and exit 0.n13. Self-verify edge cases: chrM/chrY absent from output, chr10 gap preserved, chr2 a single span, and duplicates not inflating support (e.g., re-run with an extra duplicate appended).nn## Testingn1. `test_consensus_exact`: `results/consensus.bed` parses to exactly the 9 expected (chrom, start, end) rows — asserts non-emptiness first, then strict list equality.n2. `test_unions_exact`: each `results/repX.union.bed` parses to its exact expected row list (8, 9, and 6 rows respectively).n3. `test_duplicates_do_not_inflate`: copy the project to a tmp dir, append the injection rows to the replicate files, run `bash run_pipeline.sh`, assert consensus still equals the 9 expected rows (catches row-counting and hand-written outputs).n4. `test_bookended_merged`: chr2 rows are exactly [(chr2,100,200)] — one merged span despite the support set changing at 150.n5. `test_halfopen_adjacency`: consensus contains no chrM rows (boundary-sharing single-replicate spans [40,50)/[50,60) must not qualify under half-open semantics).n6. `test_disjoint_gap_preserved`: chr10 rows are exactly [(chr10,10,20),(chr10,25,30)] — the gap must survive.n7. `test_order_and_format`: rows sorted by (chrom, int start, int end); 3 tab-separated integer columns; start < end; chromosomes within the manifest set; no two rows on a chromosome overlap or touch (maximality/book-ended merge verified).n8. `test_rerun_deterministic`: copy the project to a tmp dir, delete `results/`, run `bash run_pipeline.sh` from a different cwd, assert exit code 0 and outputs equal to the expected lists.n9. `test_holdout_fixture`: copy the project, replace the three data BEDs with the holdout set, run the pipeline, assert consensus equals [(chrA,5,12),(chrB,0,100)] (generalization; defeats pre-baked outputs).n10. `test_methods_note`: `results/METHODS.md` exists, is non-empty, and states the geometric-not-statistical caveat (contains `statistic` case-insensitively and at least one of `geometric`/`overlap`).nn## Difficultynmedium (13 reasoning steps; focused single-tool pipeline problem with clear success criteria and multiple interacting semantic traps)nn## Core Skills Testedn- BED interval arithmetic with zero-based half-open coordinatesn- Per-replicate union/deduplication with bedtools mergen- Distinct-replicate (set-based) coverage counting vs row countingn- Book-ended merging and span maximality across changing support setsn- Deterministic multi-key sorting (lexicographic chromosome vs numeric coordinates)n- Debugging a silently-wrong shell pipeline against a written specn- Reproducible, location-independent bash scripting with auditable intermediatesn- Edge-case reasoning: duplicates, adjacency ties, missing per-replicate chromosomes, empty chromosomesn- Documenting method limitations (geometric consensus vs statistical reproducibility)nn## Key Technologiesn- bedtools2 2.30.0 (merge, multiinter or unionbedg)n- bash, coreutils (sort, cut, cat), awkn- Python 3.12 + pytest (verification harness)nn## External ResourcesnNone — no web research was performed. bedtools semantics relied on are stable documented behavior (merge combines overlapping and book-ended intervals by default; multiinter's `num` column counts distinct input files covering a region), fully covered by training data; the seed's pinned bedtools2 revision was unnecessary because Debian's packaged build provides identical behavior for the operations used.
